$comment: Curated corpus of documented AI use in US political advertising. Every record must carry >=2 independent reputable sources. Deception scores are NOT stored here - they are computed from the `rubric` block by src/scoring.js so the score is always auditable against the rubric.

records.headline: NRSC ad puts a real Schumer quote into an AI-generated video of him
records.howAiUsed: The 30-second spot shows a harshly lit Schumer in the Senate halls repeating "Every day gets better for us," implying he welcomed the government shutdown. The line is a genuine Schumer quote given to Punchbowl News, but no such footage exists - the video of him delivering it was generated with AI.
records.whatIsReal: The quoted sentence was actually said by Schumer to Punchbowl News.
records.whatIsFabricated: The video itself. Schumer was never filmed saying the line in the setting shown.

disclosure.platformLabel: YouTube applied an "Altered or synthetic content" label: "Sound or visuals were significantly edited or digitally generated."

rubric.fabricationNote: Verbatim real words; only the delivery is synthetic.
rubric.realismNote: Photoreal footage a viewer could take as genuine B-roll.
rubric.disclosureNote: On-ad label present but small and easy to miss while scrolling; platform label partly mitigates.

records.headline: NRSC deepfakes James Talarico delivering a minute-long speech he never gave

depicted.name: James Talarico
depicted.role: Texas state Rep., Democratic US Senate nominee

records.howAiUsed: A photoreal AI-generated Talarico speaks directly to camera for more than a minute, reciting social-media posts he wrote years ago - including remarks on biological sex, God and Christianity - recombined and, per reporting, sometimes stripped of their original context. Talarico never filmed the video.
records.whatIsReal: The underlying sentences trace back to posts Talarico actually wrote.
records.whatIsFabricated: The speech itself. Written posts from different times were converted into a single continuous on-camera address that never happened, with context removed.

disclosure.placement: small, easy-to-miss font in the lower-right corner

rubric.fabricationNote: Scored as a fabricated performance, not merely recontextualized words: written posts were turned into a spoken address that never occurred.
rubric.realismNote: Described by reporters as real-looking; sustained photoreal talking-head footage.
rubric.disclosureNote: Label present but in small font in a corner.

records.headline: Shortsleeve campaign clones Gov. Maura Healey's voice to make her confess to a record she never described
records.howAiUsed: A mock radio spot posted to Instagram uses an AI clone of Healey's voice saying: "I'm Governor Maura Healey and I'm proud to announce my reelection campaign today... We have one of the highest electricity rates in the nation thanks to me for slapping on excessive fees to fund my climate agenda." The caption framed it as "what one of her radio ads might sound like - if she was honest."
records.whatIsReal: Nothing in the audio. The policy criticisms are the campaign's own characterization of Healey's record.
records.whatIsFabricated: Every word attributed to Healey. She never said any of it.

rubric.fabricationNote: Wholly invented words placed in a real official's cloned voice - the most direct form of putting words in someone's mouth.
rubric.realismNote: Reporters described the clone as fairly obviously artificial, but synthetic audio has no visual tells and travels well when re-shared.
rubric.disclosureNote: No AI disclosure on the artifact. The caption's framing is a partial mitigator and the campaign called it parody only after criticism; the audio carries no label if clipped and re-shared.

records.headline: Lombardo posts an AI-fabricated newspaper page showing his challenger hand-in-hand with Mamdani

depicted.name: Daniel Darris-O'Connor
depicted.role: Challenger for the Billerica House seat

records.howAiUsed: A Facebook post presents an AI-generated image styled as an old-fashioned newspaper article, showing challenger Daniel Darris-O'Connor joining hands with New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani - at what Axios described as "the sort of physically impossible angle AI image generators are known for" - to tie the challenger to Mamdani's democratic-socialist politics.
records.whatIsReal: The policy association the ad argues for is the sponsor's own claim.
records.whatIsFabricated: The photograph and the newspaper page. The depicted meeting never happened and the publication does not exist.

rubric.fabricationNote: Depicts an association and an event that never occurred, and imitates a news artifact - but attributes no spoken words.
rubric.realismNote: Obvious generation artifacts and a stylized period-newspaper frame; unlikely to be mistaken for a real photograph on inspection.
rubric.disclosureNote: No AI disclosure of any kind.

records.headline: Paxton's first ad shows an AI Cornyn dancing with Jasmine Crockett
records.howAiUsed: Paxton's opening primary ad uses AI-generated video of Sen. John Cornyn dancing with Rep. Jasmine Crockett while a narrator says: "Publicly, they're opponents. Privately, they're perfectly in step."
records.whatIsReal: The voting-record argument the narrator makes is the campaign's own characterization.
records.whatIsFabricated: The dancing footage. Cornyn and Crockett were never filmed together this way.

disclosure.wording: satire that does not represent real events
disclosure.placement: small font at the end of the ad

rubric.fabricationNote: Shows two real officials doing something they never did; no words are put in their mouths.
rubric.realismNote: Video-realistic but the scenario reads as visual metaphor rather than documentary footage.
rubric.disclosureNote: Explicitly says it is not a real event - stronger wording than a bare 'AI generated' tag - but set in small type at the end.

records.headline: Cornyn answers with an AI video of Paxton driving with "Mistress #1" and "Mistress #2"
records.howAiUsed: Released in response to Paxton's dancing ad, Cornyn's spot uses AI-generated video of Paxton driving a convertible with two women captioned "Mistress #1" and "Mistress #2," invoking infidelity allegations that have followed Paxton through the race.
records.whatIsReal: The infidelity allegations referenced are a matter of prior public reporting.
records.whatIsFabricated: The scene. No such footage of Paxton exists.

rubric.fabricationNote: Depicts a real official in a staged scene that never occurred.
rubric.realismNote: Realistic rendering, but the captioned-passenger device signals construction.
rubric.disclosureNote: PROVISIONAL: a campaign-level satire disclosure was reported, but later reporting found a separate Cornyn AI ad carrying no disclosure at all, so it cannot be assumed here. Scored as absent.

records.headline: Texas House candidate's satire video clones her opponent's voice alongside deepfaked Putin and Xi
records.howAiUsed: A satirical YouTube video attacking Rep. Angelia Orr's voting record uses AI deepfakes of Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping together with synthetic voice clones and manipulated visuals of Orr, framing her as an ally of foreign adversaries.
records.whatIsReal: The voting-record claims are the sponsor's characterization of Orr's public votes.
records.whatIsFabricated: The depictions of all three figures, including audio attributed to Orr.

rubric.fabricationNote: Audio attributed to a real opponent that she never spoke.
rubric.realismNote: Broad satire - the Putin/Xi framing signals fiction immediately.
rubric.disclosureNote: PROVISIONAL: no disclosure confirmed in available reporting. Scored as absent pending verification, which is the harshest reading.

records.headline: Crockett posts an AI video casting herself as a baby confronting "Baby Trump"
records.howAiUsed: Crockett posted an AI-generated video to her Facebook page portraying herself as a baby accusing a "Baby Trump" character of rigging Texas elections.
records.whatIsReal: The election-rigging accusation is Crockett's own stated position.
records.whatIsFabricated: The entire scene, rendered as caricature.

rubric.fabricationNote: The sponsor depicts herself, with consent; the opposing figure appears as an infant caricature rather than a realistic likeness. Included as a low-end reference point for what routine, non-deceptive AI use looks like.
rubric.realismNote: Cartoon caricature; no viewer would read it as footage.
rubric.disclosureNote: No label, though the format is self-evidently synthetic.

records.headline: Mike Collins' campaign deepfakes Jon Ossoff mocking farmers and backing the shutdown
records.howAiUsed: Rep. Mike Collins' Senate campaign released a deepfake video of Sen. Jon Ossoff, with computer-generated audio in Ossoff's voice, showing him defending the government shutdown and mocking farmers — including a line about having "only seen a farm on Instagram."
records.whatIsReal: Nothing in the video. The policy position attributed to Ossoff is the sponsor's characterization.
records.whatIsFabricated: Ossoff's image, his voice, and every word attributed to him. He never said any of it.

rubric.fabricationNote: Invented words in a real senator's cloned voice and likeness.
rubric.realismNote: Photoreal video with synthetic audio matched to the real person.
rubric.disclosureNote: A disclaimer is present — the campaign said it was included specifically to stay within Georgia and federal law — but it is small and on-screen only.

records.headline: Oregon opens a disclosure-law investigation into unlabeled AI videos of Rep. Janelle Bynum
records.howAiUsed: During his unsuccessful primary run, Jonathan Lockwood posted a series of AI videos depicting Rep. Janelle Bynum — in one, handing the keys to a girls' locker room to a drag queen and saying "Don't let me down"; in another, Bynum and Gov. Tina Kotek menacing terrified children in an apparent Satanic ritual. None carried an AI label.
records.whatIsFabricated: Every depicted scene, action and line of dialogue.

rubric.fabricationNote: Invented both words and acts for two real officials.
rubric.realismNote: Reported as over-the-top and absurd; Lockwood's own defense to state officials is that no one could mistake them for real.
rubric.disclosureNote: No AI label — the omission is the basis of the state investigation, which carries fines up to $10,000.

sources.title: Over-the-top AI campaign ads will test Oregon disclosure law

records.legalNote: Under investigation by the Oregon Secretary of State for violating the state's 2024 AI disclosure statute. Lockwood denies violating any Oregon law. No finding has been made.

records.headline: NRSC ad stages an AI Graham Platner giving a shirtless "dramatic reading" of his old Reddit posts
records.howAiUsed: The NRSC ad, titled as a "dramatic reading of Graham Platner's Reddit comments," uses an AI-generated image and an AI voice of a shirtless Platner reciting Reddit posts he wrote 10 to 15 years ago.
records.whatIsReal: The Reddit posts are Platner's own; he has acknowledged writing them and said he regrets them.
records.whatIsFabricated: The reading itself, his voice, and the shirtless depiction. Platner never performed any of it.

rubric.fabricationNote: The words are genuinely his; the ad's own title frames it as a staged reading rather than real footage. The invented shirtless staging pushes past a plain re-voicing.
rubric.realismNote: A synthetic still and voice rather than photoreal motion footage.
rubric.disclosureNote: PROVISIONAL: no on-ad label confirmed in available reporting. Scored as absent, the harshest reading; the ad's title does signal construction.

records.headline: Cornyn posts an undisclosed AI video casting Rep. Wesley Hunt as a show dog
records.howAiUsed: Sen. John Cornyn posted an AI-generated video depicting primary rival Rep. Wesley Hunt as a "show dog." Reporters noted it was markedly more sophisticated than earlier AI ads in the race and carried no disclosure; AI-detection tools returned a 99% probability the video was machine-generated, with tells including blurred background signage, an oddly folded US flag and unnatural movement.
records.whatIsReal: The rivalry and the criticism are real; the footage is not.
records.whatIsFabricated: The entire scene and Hunt's depiction in it.

rubric.fabricationNote: Places a real congressman in a staged scene that never happened; no words are attributed to him.
rubric.realismNote: Polished enough to fool a scroll, but the premise is caricature and detection tools find clear artifacts.
rubric.disclosureNote: No disclosure of any kind, in contrast to the labeled satire card used on other ads in the same race.
